1. Core Clinical Tension: A pediatric patient hospitalized in a bone marrow transplant unit developing fever on day +26 post-haploidentical transplant with elevated inflammatory markers and intercurrent bacterial bacteriuria. The key tension is identifying a secondary viral infection presenting with biphasic fever and plasma leak syndrome when initial viral testing was completely negative.
2. Admission Breakpoint: The presentation ends at the initial fever spike on post-transplant day +26 with elevated C-reactive protein and procalcitonin, immediately prior to send-out cultures, viral/fungal panels, second fever spike, and serologic testing.
3. Differential Distinctions: Distinguishing acute arboviral plasma leak syndrome from persistent bacterial sepsis/pyelonephritis (E. coli isolated in urine), invasive mold infection/galactomannan positivity, CMV reactivation, and BKV-associated hemorrhagic cystitis.
case_prompt: An 8-year-old child admitted to the transplant unit for a haploidentical stem cell transplant for beta-thalassemia major developed a sudden fever spike on day +26 post-transplant. Baseline triage laboratory investigations revealed markedly elevated inflammatory markers, including high C-reactive protein and procalcitonin.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Although Escherichia coli was cultured from urine and targeted antibiotics were administered, the patient suffered a subsequent fever spike and vascular leakage inconsistent with treated bacterial infection alone.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: He grew Escherichia coli in urine culture with raised C-reactive protein and procalcitonin.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Opportunistic Viral (CMV, BKV) or Fungal (Aspergillosis) Infection / Malaria
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered due to post-transplant immunosuppression, but extensive microbiological testing for opportunistic pathogens returned negative.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Laboratory workup was negative for dengue NS1, malarial parasite, galactomanan, BKV, and Cytomegalovirus (CMV).

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Emergence of positive serology at a recurrent fever spike accompanied by objective third-space fluid accumulation (plasma leak syndrome) on thoracic and abdominal imaging confirmed severe dengue.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Second fever spike occurred 4 days later and that time dengue serology turned out to be positive. He also developed features of plasma leak syndrome confirmed on ultrasound of whole abdomen and chest X-ray.

editor_comments: Distilled admission teaching case for Dengue virus infection with plasma leak syndrome. Zero spoilers, culture results, or second fever spike in case_prompt. Exact quotes matched.
